claim: CaV-channel dependent activation of BK channels is critical for feedback control of both calcium influx and cell excitability.
source: CaV-channel dependent activation of BK channels is critical for feedback control of both calcium influx and cell excitability.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific understanding about the functional relationship between CaV and BK channels.

claim: When BK and CaV1.3 channels were co-expressed in the same cell, BK channels started activating near −50 mV.
source: We found that when BK and CaV1.3 channels were co-expressed in the same cell, BK channels started activating near −50 mV, ~30 mV more negative than for activation of co-expressed BK and high-voltage activated CaV2.2 channels.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from co-expression studies shown in Figure 1.

claim: BK channels co-expressed with CaV1.3 activate ~30 mV more negative than BK channels co-expressed with CaV2.2 channels.
source: We found that when BK and CaV1.3 channels were co-expressed in the same cell, BK channels started activating near −50 mV, ~30 mV more negative than for activation of co-expressed BK and high-voltage activated CaV2.2 channels.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison based on experimental measurements shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Single-molecule localization microscopy revealed striking clusters of CaV1.3 channels surrounding clusters of BK channels in a heterologous system.
source: In addition, single-molecule localization microscopy revealed striking clusters of CaV1.3 channels surrounding clusters of BK channels and forming a multi-channel complex both in a heterologous system and in rat hippocampal and sympathetic neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Single-molecule localization microscopy revealed striking clusters of CaV1.3 channels surrounding clusters of BK channels in rat hippocampal neurons.
source: In addition, single-molecule localization microscopy revealed striking clusters of CaV1.3 channels surrounding clusters of BK channels and forming a multi-channel complex both in a heterologous system and in rat hippocampal and sympathetic neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Single-molecule localization microscopy revealed striking clusters of CaV1.3 channels surrounding clusters of BK channels in rat sympathetic neurons.
source: In addition, single-molecule localization microscopy revealed striking clusters of CaV1.3 channels surrounding clusters of BK channels and forming a multi-channel complex both in a heterologous system and in rat hippocampal and sympathetic neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The spatial arrangement between BK and CaV1.3 channels allows tight tracking between local BK channel activation and the gating of CaV1.3 channels at quite negative membrane potentials.
source: We propose that this spatial arrangement allows tight tracking between local BK channel activation and the gating of CaV1.3 channels at quite negative membrane potentials, facilitating the regulation of neuronal excitability at voltages close to the threshold to fire action potentials.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings of spatial proximity and functional coupling.

claim: The spatial arrangement between BK and CaV1.3 channels facilitates the regulation of neuronal excitability at voltages close to the threshold to fire action potentials.
source: We propose that this spatial arrangement allows tight tracking between local BK channel activation and the gating of CaV1.3 channels at quite negative membrane potentials, facilitating the regulation of neuronal excitability at voltages close to the threshold to fire action potentials.
evidence: This is a proposed physiological consequence based on the experimental findings.

claim: BK channels are expressed in nearly every excitable cell.
source: BK channels are expressed in nearly every excitable cell and their activation depends on both voltage and intracellular calcium (Cui et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BK channel activation depends on both voltage and intracellular calcium.
source: BK channels are expressed in nearly every excitable cell and their activation depends on both voltage and intracellular calcium (Cui et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Without calcium ([Ca2+]i = 0), BK channels activate only at very depolarized voltages with a V1/2 >100 mV.
source: Without calcium ([Ca2+]i = 0), BK channels activate only at very depolarized voltages with a V1/2 >100 mV (Yan and Aldrich, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The affinity of BK channels for calcium ions ranges between 1 and 10 μM.
source: The affinity of BK channels for calcium ions ranges between 1 and 10 μM (Contreras et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: A rise in calcium concentration from ~100 nM resting levels to the micromolar range is needed to increase the open-channel probability of BK channels at −50 to 0 mV.
source: Therefore, a rise in calcium concentration from ~100 nM resting levels to the micromolar range is needed to increase the open-channel probability of BK channels at −50 to 0 mV (Barrett et al., 1982).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature and represents an inference from the calcium affinity data.

claim: Opening of a single calcium channel raises local calcium to more than 100 μM within a few tens of nanometers from the inner mouth of the channel.
source: Opening of a single calcium channel raises local calcium to more than 100 μM within a few tens of nanometers from the inner mouth of the channel, but most of these ions are quickly buffered--within microseconds (Simon and Llinás, 1985; Roberts, 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Most calcium ions entering through a single calcium channel are quickly buffered within microseconds.
source: Opening of a single calcium channel raises local calcium to more than 100 μM within a few tens of nanometers from the inner mouth of the channel, but most of these ions are quickly buffered--within microseconds (Simon and Llinás, 1985; Roberts, 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BK channels have been found in close proximity to all subfamilies of CaV channels.
source: BK channels have been found in close proximity to all subfamilies of CaV channels, suggesting a molecular interaction (Roberts et al., 1990; Roberts, 1994; Marrion and Tavalin, 1998; Berkefeld and Fakler, 2008; Müller et al., 2010; Rehak et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: The proximity of BK channels to all subfamilies of CaV channels suggests a molecular interaction.
source: BK channels have been found in close proximity to all subfamilies of CaV channels, suggesting a molecular interaction (Roberts et al., 1990; Roberts, 1994; Marrion and Tavalin, 1998; Berkefeld and Fakler, 2008; Müller et al., 2010; Rehak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed proximity, supported by citations.

claim: The association between BK and CaV channels can be recapitulated in heterologous systems.
source: This association can be recapitulated in heterologous systems and has been shown to reconstitute functional nanodomains (Berkefeld et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The association between BK and CaV channels has been shown to reconstitute functional nanodomains.
source: This association can be recapitulated in heterologous systems and has been shown to reconstitute functional nanodomains (Berkefeld et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Some models depict a 1:1 relation between CaV and BK channels arranged at distances as close as 10 nm.
source: Some models depict a 1:1 relation between CaV and BK channels arranged at distances as close as 10 nm (Fakler and Adelman, 2008; Cox, 2014).
evidence: This claim describes existing models in the literature, supported by citations.

claim: Other models are similarly effective in reproducing the functional coupling without a 1:1 stoichiometry.
source: Other models are similarly effective in reproducing the functional coupling without a 1:1 stoichiometry (Prakriya and Lingle, 2000; Montefusco et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim describes alternative models in the literature, supported by citations.

claim: The activation threshold of BK channels tends to reflect the activation threshold of associated CaV partners.
source: The activation threshold of BK channels tends to reflect the activation threshold of associated CaV partners.
evidence: This is a general principle based on established knowledge of BK-CaV coupling.

claim: CaV1.3 channels can start activating at voltages as negative as −65 mV.
source: Dihydropyridine-sensitive, L-type CaV1.3 channels are unique in their activation profile; they can start activating at voltages as negative as −65 mV (Platzer et al., 2000; Lipscombe et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CaV1.3 channels play essential roles in the auditory system.
source: These channels play essential roles in the auditory system (Koschak et al., 2001; Michna et al., 2003; Brandt et al., 2003, 2005), in the pacemaker cells of the heart (Mangoni et al., 2003; Christel et al., 2012; Torrente et al., 2016), in chromaffin cells (Marcantoni et al., 2010), and in neurons (Putzier et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2014; Cooper et al., 2015; Lu et al., 2015; Stanika et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: CaV1.3 channels play essential roles in the pacemaker cells of the heart.
source: These channels play essential roles in the auditory system (Koschak et al., 2001; Michna et al., 2003; Brandt et al., 2003, 2005), in the pacemaker cells of the heart (Mangoni et al., 2003; Christel et al., 2012; Torrente et al., 2016), in chromaffin cells (Marcantoni et al., 2010), and in neurons (Putzier et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2014; Cooper et al., 2015; Lu et al., 2015; Stanika et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: CaV1.3 channels play essential roles in chromaffin cells.
source: These channels play essential roles in the auditory system (Koschak et al., 2001; Michna et al., 2003; Brandt et al., 2003, 2005), in the pacemaker cells of the heart (Mangoni et al., 2003; Christel et al., 2012; Torrente et al., 2016), in chromaffin cells (Marcantoni et al., 2010), and in neurons (Putzier et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2014; Cooper et al., 2015; Lu et al., 2015; Stanika et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: CaV1.3 channels play essential roles in neurons.
source: These channels play essential roles in the auditory system (Koschak et al., 2001; Michna et al., 2003; Brandt et al., 2003, 2005), in the pacemaker cells of the heart (Mangoni et al., 2003; Christel et al., 2012; Torrente et al., 2016), in chromaffin cells (Marcantoni et al., 2010), and in neurons (Putzier et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2014; Cooper et al., 2015; Lu et al., 2015; Stanika et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Deficiency of CaV1.3 channels leads to deafness and bradycardia.
source: Deficiency of CaV1.3 channels leads to deafness and bradycardia (Platzer et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Coupling between BK and CaV1.3 channels can activate BK channels at very negative voltages.
source: Here, we tested the hypothesis that coupling between these channels can activate BK channels at very negative voltages.
evidence: This is the main hypothesis tested in the study, supported by experimental data in Figures 1 and 5.

claim: BK-channel opening would oppose further opening of CaV1.3 channels even before the membrane potential reaches the firing threshold for action potentials.
source: This would promote a negative feedback mechanism whereby BK-channel opening would oppose further opening of CaV1.3 channels even before the membrane potential reaches the firing threshold for action potentials.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings, representing an inference about the physiological consequence.

claim: To activate BK channels at low voltages, the CaV1.3 and BK channels must be organized in close proximity (<20 nm).
source: In order to activate BK channels at these low voltages, the CaV1.3 and BK channels must be organized in close proximity (<20 nm), so that nanodomains of calcium forming near the inner mouth of the calcium channel overlap with the calcium sensors of the BK channel.
evidence: This is a theoretical requirement based on calcium diffusion and buffering, supported by the experimental data with BAPTA and EGTA in Figure 3.

claim: tsA-201 cells do not express BK channels endogenously.
source: These cells do not express BK or any of the isoforms of CaV channels endogenously (Berjukow et al., 1996; Zhu et al., 1998; Avila et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: tsA-201 cells do not express any isoforms of CaV channels endogenously.
source: These cells do not express BK or any of the isoforms of CaV channels endogenously (Berjukow et al., 1996; Zhu et al., 1998; Avila et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The inward calcium currents from cells expressing only CaV2.2 or CaV1.3 are blocked by cadmium.
source: As expected, the inward calcium currents from cells expressing only CaV2.2 or CaV1.3 (Figure 1A) are blocked by cadmium, a general blocker of CaV channels, but they differ in their gating kinetics.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: CaV2.2 and CaV1.3 channels differ in their gating kinetics.
source: As expected, the inward calcium currents from cells expressing only CaV2.2 or CaV1.3 (Figure 1A) are blocked by cadmium, a general blocker of CaV channels, but they differ in their gating kinetics.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: The midpoint of activation of the CaV1.3 channels is 35 mV more negative than that for the CaV2.2 channels.
source: The midpoint of activation of the CaV1.3 channels is 35 mV more negative than that for the CaV2.2 channels.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Outward K+ currents from cells expressing only BK channels are insignificant in the voltage range used.
source: Outward K+ currents from cells expressing only BK channels are insignificant in the voltage range that we used (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: When CaV channels are co-expressed with BK channels, voltage steps elicit an outward current that is blocked by cadmium.
source: When CaV channels are co-expressed with the BK channels, the same voltage steps elicit an outward current that is blocked by cadmium (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Calcium influx through CaV isoforms is required for the activation of BK channels in the expression system.
source: These results confirm that calcium influx through CaV isoforms is required for the activation of BK channels in the expression system.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cadmium-sensitivity experiments shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: The mid-point voltage for activation of BK channels depends on the co-expressed CaV channel isoform.
source: As anticipated, the mid-point voltage for activation of BK channels depends on the co-expressed CaV channel isoform (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The activation threshold for CaV2.2 channels was −13.8 mV.
source: In this terminology, the activation threshold for CaV2.2 channels was −13.8 mV and for the co-expressed BK channels it was −20.2 mV, whereas for CaV1.3 channels the activation threshold was −48.8 mV and for the co-expressed BK channels it was −52.3 mV.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from the Boltzmann fits in Figure 1B.

claim: The activation threshold for BK channels co-expressed with CaV2.2 was −20.2 mV.
source: In this terminology, the activation threshold for CaV2.2 channels was −13.8 mV and for the co-expressed BK channels it was −20.2 mV, whereas for CaV1.3 channels the activation threshold was −48.8 mV and for the co-expressed BK channels it was −52.3 mV.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from the Boltzmann fits in Figure 1E.

claim: The activation threshold for CaV1.3 channels was −48.8 mV.
source: In this terminology, the activation threshold for CaV2.2 channels was −13.8 mV and for the co-expressed BK channels it was −20.2 mV, whereas for CaV1.3 channels the activation threshold was −48.8 mV and for the co-expressed BK channels it was −52.3 mV.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from the Boltzmann fits in Figure 1B.

claim: The activation threshold for BK channels co-expressed with CaV1.3 was −52.3 mV.
source: In this terminology, the activation threshold for CaV2.2 channels was −13.8 mV and for the co-expressed BK channels it was −20.2 mV, whereas for CaV1.3 channels the activation threshold was −48.8 mV and for the co-expressed BK channels it was −52.3 mV.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from the Boltzmann fits in Figure 1E.

claim: The activation kinetics of BK channels changes when coupled with different CaV isoforms.
source: The activation kinetics of BK channels has also been shown to change when coupled with different CaV isoforms (Berkefeld and Fakler, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The time constant of BK channel activation at 0 mV is shorter when co-expressed with CaV1.3 (8 ± 2 ms, n = 7) than when co-expressed with CaV2.2 channels (18 ± 5 ms, n = 9).
source: In agreement, the time constant of BK channel activation at 0 mV is shorter when co-expressed with CaV1.3 (8 ± 2 ms, n = 7) than when is co-expressed with CaV2.2 channels (18 ± 5, n = 9), resembling the difference in activation kinetics between CaV1.3 (0.7 ± 0.1 ms, n = 9) and CaV2.2 (4.5 ± 0.7 ms, n = 8) channels (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The activation time constant of CaV1.3 channels at 0 mV is 0.7 ± 0.1 ms (n = 9).
source: In agreement, the time constant of BK channel activation at 0 mV is shorter when co-expressed with CaV1.3 (8 ± 2 ms, n = 7) than when is co-expressed with CaV2.2 channels (18 ± 5, n = 9), resembling the difference in activation kinetics between CaV1.3 (0.7 ± 0.1 ms, n = 9) and CaV2.2 (4.5 ± 0.7 ms, n = 8) channels (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The activation time constant of CaV2.2 channels at 0 mV is 4.5 ± 0.7 ms (n = 8).
source: In agreement, the time constant of BK channel activation at 0 mV is shorter when co-expressed with CaV1.3 (8 ± 2 ms, n = 7) than when is co-expressed with CaV2.2 channels (18 ± 5, n = 9), resembling the difference in activation kinetics between CaV1.3 (0.7 ± 0.1 ms, n = 9) and CaV2.2 (4.5 ± 0.7 ms, n = 8) channels (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Unitary outward K+ currents with multiple levels were recorded from membrane patches of cells co-expressing BK and CaV1.3 channels.
source: Indeed, unitary outward K+ currents with multiple levels were recorded from these patches (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 for raw trace), reflecting the activation of CaV1.3 channels and subsequent activation of BK channels.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: NPo in membrane patches from cells co-expressing BK and CaV1.3 channels was 3.7 ± 0.7 (n = 8).
source: NPo in these patches was 3.7 ± 0.7 (n = 8, Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: NPo decreased to 0.8 ± 0.4 (n = 7, p value = 0.002) after bath application of nifedipine (10 μM).
source: NPo decreased to 0.8 ± 0.4 (n = 7, p value = 0.002) after bath application of the dihydropyridine blocker nifedipine (10 μM) suggesting that CaV1.3 channels need to be activated to induce these outward current events.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CaV1.3 channels need to be activated to induce BK channel outward current events.
source: NPo decreased to 0.8 ± 0.4 (n = 7, p value = 0.002) after bath application of the dihydropyridine blocker nifedipine (10 μM) suggesting that CaV1.3 channels need to be activated to induce these outward current events.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effect of nifedipine on NPo.

claim: NPo decreased to 0.2 ± 0.1 (n = 7, p value = 0.0004) after the sequential application of paxilline (500 nM).
source: Openings were abolished and NPo decreased to 0.2 ± 0.1 (n = 7, p value = 0.0004) after the sequential application of a BK channel blocker, 500 nM paxilline, confirming the identity of BK channels coupled with CaV1.3 channels (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: BK and CaV1.3 channels co-immunoprecipitate from brain extracts.
source: CaV1.3 and BK channels have been previously shown to co-immunoprecipitate from brain extracts (Grunnet and Kaufmann, 2004), suggesting a direct interaction.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The co-immunoprecipitation of BK and CaV1.3 channels from brain extracts suggests a direct interaction.
source: CaV1.3 and BK channels have been previously shown to co-immunoprecipitate from brain extracts (Grunnet and Kaufmann, 2004), suggesting a direct interaction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-immunoprecipitation result.

claim: BK antibody stains immunoprecipitates pulled down with CaV1.3 antibodies from tsA-201 cells transfected with both BK and CaV1.3 channels.
source: The BK antibody also stains immunoprecipitates pulled down with CaV1.3 antibodies (n = 3, Figure 2C, right gel), suggesting that some level of interaction between these channels is reconstituted when expressed in a heterologous system and that no other proteins specific to brain tissue are required for this interaction.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Some level of interaction between BK and CaV1.3 channels is reconstituted when expressed in a heterologous system.
source: The BK antibody also stains immunoprecipitates pulled down with CaV1.3 antibodies (n = 3, Figure 2C, right gel), suggesting that some level of interaction between these channels is reconstituted when expressed in a heterologous system and that no other proteins specific to brain tissue are required for this interaction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-immunoprecipitation result from tsA-201 cells.

claim: No other proteins specific to brain tissue are required for the interaction between BK and CaV1.3 channels.
source: The BK antibody also stains immunoprecipitates pulled down with CaV1.3 antibodies (n = 3, Figure 2C, right gel), suggesting that some level of interaction between these channels is reconstituted when expressed in a heterologous system and that no other proteins specific to brain tissue are required for this interaction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the successful reconstitution in tsA-201 cells.

claim: Dialysis of 10 mM EGTA restricts local elevations of intracellular calcium to a radius of 100 nm from the calcium source.
source: The equation of Prakriya and Lingle, 2000, predicts that dialysis of 10 mM EGTA restricts local elevations of intracellular calcium to a radius of 100 nm from the calcium source, whereas dialysis of 10 mM BAPTA restricts diffusion to a radius of 10 nm (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is based on a theoretical prediction from a cited equation.

claim: Dialysis of 10 mM BAPTA restricts local elevations of intracellular calcium to a radius of 10 nm from the calcium source.
source: The equation of Prakriya and Lingle, 2000, predicts that dialysis of 10 mM EGTA restricts local elevations of intracellular calcium to a radius of 100 nm from the calcium source, whereas dialysis of 10 mM BAPTA restricts diffusion to a radius of 10 nm (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is based on a theoretical prediction from a cited equation.

claim: Potassium currents activated by CaV1.3 channels were reduced by dialysis with BAPTA but not EGTA.
source: Tellingly, potassium currents activated by CaV1.3 channels were reduced by dialysis with BAPTA but not EGTA (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Some BK channels lie closer than 10 nm to CaV1.3 channels.
source: Interestingly, some current remains even with the dialysis of BAPTA, suggesting that some BK channels lie closer than 10 nm to CaV1.3 channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the incomplete block by BAPTA shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Potassium currents were reduced by dialysis of either BAPTA or EGTA in tsA-201 cells co-expressing BK and CaV2.2 channels.
source: In contrast, potassium currents were reduced by dialysis of either BAPTA or EGTA in tsA-201 cells co-expressing BK and CaV2.2 channels (Figure 3C), suggesting that BK channels are distributed farther than 100 nm from CaV2.2 channels.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: BK channels are distributed farther than 100 nm from CaV2.2 channels.
source: In contrast, potassium currents were reduced by dialysis of either BAPTA or EGTA in tsA-201 cells co-expressing BK and CaV2.2 channels (Figure 3C), suggesting that BK channels are distributed farther than 100 nm from CaV2.2 channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effect of EGTA on BK currents coupled to CaV2.2.

claim: BK and CaV1.3 channels organize in close proximity, creating a functional unit with preferential co-localization in a range of less than 100 nm.
source: These observations imply that BK and CaV1.3 channels organize in close proximity, creating a functional unit with preferential co-localization in a range of less than 100 nm.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the calcium buffer experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Single microtubules exhibit a full-width-at-half-maximum of 33 ± 1 nm in super-resolution microscopy.
source: In agreement with previous reports (Burnette et al., 2011), these single microtubules exhibit a full-width-at-half-maximum of 33 ± 1 nm.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and agrees with cited literature.

claim: BK channels form multi-pixel aggregates with a median area of 1600 nm2 in tsA-201 cells (n = 5 cells).
source: In Figure 4A, pixels positive for BK channels (red) formed multi-pixel aggregates, with a median area of 1600 nm2 (n = 5 cells).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: BK channel aggregates are much larger than the expected size for a single ion channel.
source: They are much larger than the expected size for a single ion channel, which has known dimensions of 13 by 13 nm (Wang and Sigworth, 2009; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison between measured aggregate size and known single channel dimensions from cited literature.

claim: BK channel aggregates are interpreted as clusters of multiple BK channels.
source: Therefore, we interpreted these aggregates as clusters of multiple BK channels.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the size comparison.

claim: Clusters of BK channels are surrounded by variable numbers of clusters of CaV1.3 channels.
source: In numerous cases, the clusters of BK channels (red) were surrounded by variable numbers of clusters of CaV1.3 channels (green) rather than showing any fixed stoichiometry or geometry (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Only 18 ± 5% of the BK clusters were not surrounded by CaV1.3 clusters within a radius of 200 nm (n = 5 cells).
source: Only 18 ± 5% of the BK clusters were not surrounded by CaV1.3 clusters within a radius of 200 nm (n = 5 cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the super-resolution data.

claim: The frequency distribution of the distance between CaV1.3 and BK-positive pixels was empirically fitted by a bell-shaped curve with a peak at 20 nm and a half width of 60 nm.
source: The frequency distribution for the distance between CaV1.3 and BK-positive pixels (Figure 4C, green bars) was empirically fitted by a bell-shaped curve with a peak at 20 nm, our resolution limit, and a half width of 60 nm.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CaV1.3 channels show a skewed distribution towards areas within 50 nm from BK clusters.
source: This plot shows a skewed distribution of CaV1.3 channels towards areas within 50 nm from BK clusters, indicating again that CaV1.3 clusters are preferentially concentrated in close proximity to BK clusters.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Only 17 ± 2% of CaV1.3 clusters are at <200 nm from BK channels while 83% of CaV1.3 clusters are not localized close to any BK cluster (n = 5 cells).
source: Importantly, only 17 ± 2% of CaV1.3 clusters are at <200 nm from BK channels while the other 83% of CaV1.3 clusters are not localized close to any BK cluster (n = 5 cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the super-resolution data.

claim: Live cells exhibited BK channel puncta surrounded by CaV1.3 channel puncta.
source: Similar to what we observed in fixed cells, live cells exhibited BK channel puncta surrounded by CaV1.3 channel puncta (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The median BK cluster size is not significantly different when BK channels are co-expressed with CaV2.2 channels (2000 nm2, n = 4 cells).
source: The median BK cluster size is not significantly different when BK channels are co-expressed with CaV2.2 channels (2000 nm2, n = 4 cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of cluster sizes.

claim: There is much less evidence for an association of CaV2.2 with BK channels compared to CaV1.3.
source: In comparison to the results with CaV1.3 channels, there is much less evidence for an association of CaV2.2 with BK channels.
evidence: This is a comparative conclusion based on the super-resolution data in Figure 4.

claim: The frequency distribution for the distance between CaV2.2 and BK-positive pixels is roughly described by a bell-shaped curve centered at 100 nm from BK-positive pixels.
source: The frequency distribution for the distance between CaV2.2 and BK-positive pixels is roughly described by a bell-shaped curve centered at 100 nm from BK-positive pixels (Figure 4C, cyan bars).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CaV2.2-positive pixels are more randomly distributed around BK channels.
source: In addition, CaV2.2-positive pixels are more randomly distributed around BK channels (Figure 4D, cyan circles).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: CaV1.3 channels are more likely to be close to BK channels than are CaV2.2 channels in the heterologous expression system.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that CaV1.3 channels are more likely to be close to BK channels than are CaV2.2 channels in our heterologous expression system.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparative super-resolution data in Figure 4.

claim: There were 2.5 times more CaV1.3 clusters (1843 ± 587) than CaV2.2 clusters (741 ± 273) in the super-resolution maps.
source: In the super-resolution maps, there were 2.5 times more CaV1.3 clusters (1843 ± 587) with a median cluster size of 1600 nm2 than CaV2.2 clusters (741 ± 273) with a median cluster size of 400 nm2.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of cluster numbers from the super-resolution data.

claim: The peak inward current density was −38 ± 11 pA/pF (n = 11) in cells co-transfected with CaV1.3.
source: The peak inward current density was −38 ± 11 pA/pF (n = 11) in cells co-transfected with CaV1.3 and only −10 ± 3 pA/pF (n = 9) in cells co-transfected with CaV2.2 (p=0.04).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of current density.

claim: The peak inward current density was −10 ± 3 pA/pF (n = 9) in cells co-transfected with CaV2.2.
source: The peak inward current density was −38 ± 11 pA/pF (n = 11) in cells co-transfected with CaV1.3 and only −10 ± 3 pA/pF (n = 9) in cells co-transfected with CaV2.2 (p=0.04).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of current density.

claim: The distribution curve of randomized CaV1.3 pixels did not depend on the position of BK clusters.
source: The distribution curve of randomized CaV1.3 pixels did not depend on the position of BK clusters (Figure 4D, orange circles), being more similar to the distribution observed for CaV2.2 channels.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: A higher expression level of CaV1.3 channels alone does not account for the greater coupling with BK channels.
source: This result rejects the possibility that a higher expression level of CaV1.3 channels alone accounts for the greater coupling with BK channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the randomization analysis shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: Hippocampal neurons abundantly express BK and CaV1.3 channels.
source: Hippocampal and sympathetic neurons abundantly express BK and CaV1.3 channels, where they are known to serve important physiological functions (Storm, 1987; Lancaster and Nicoll, 1987; Gu et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sympathetic neurons abundantly express BK and CaV1.3 channels.

claim: BK and CaV1.3 channels serve important physiological functions in hippocampal and sympathetic neurons.
source: Hippocampal and sympathetic neurons abundantly express BK and CaV1.3 channels, where they are known to serve important physiological functions (Storm, 1987; Lancaster and Nicoll, 1987; Gu et al., 2007).

claim: The overlap between CaV1.3 and CaV1.2 antibody labels is only 2.2 ± 0.5% (n = 4).
source: In fact, the overlap between the two labels is only 2.2 ± 0.5% (n = 4), supporting that the antibody used against CaV1.3 channels does not recognize CaV1.2 channels.

claim: The antibody used against CaV1.3 channels does not recognize CaV1.2 channels.
source: In fact, the overlap between the two labels is only 2.2 ± 0.5% (n = 4), supporting that the antibody used against CaV1.3 channels does not recognize CaV1.2 channels.

claim: BK channels formed clusters surrounded by clusters of CaV1.3 channels in hippocampal neurons.
source: Similar to the distribution observed in the heterologous expression system, BK channels formed clusters surrounded by clusters of CaV1.3 channels (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: BK channels formed clusters surrounded by clusters of CaV1.3 channels in sympathetic neurons.
source: Similar to the distribution observed in the heterologous expression system, BK channels formed clusters surrounded by clusters of CaV1.3 channels (Figure 5A,B).

claim: The BK-CaV1.3 clustering organization was not dependent on the secondary antibody used.
source: The BK-CaV1.3 clustering organization was not dependent on the secondary antibody used (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The median BK cluster size is 2800 nm2 in SCG neurons (n = 7).
source: The median BK cluster size is 2800 nm2 in SCG neurons (n = 7), significantly larger than the median BK cluster size in hippocampal neurons (2000 nm2, n = 6) or the expression system (1600 nm2, n = 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the super-resolution data.

claim: The median BK cluster size in SCG neurons is significantly larger than in hippocampal neurons (2000 nm2, n = 6).
source: The median BK cluster size is 2800 nm2 in SCG neurons (n = 7), significantly larger than the median BK cluster size in hippocampal neurons (2000 nm2, n = 6) or the expression system (1600 nm2, n = 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison from the super-resolution data.

claim: The median BK cluster size in SCG neurons is significantly larger than in the expression system (1600 nm2, n = 5).
source: The median BK cluster size is 2800 nm2 in SCG neurons (n = 7), significantly larger than the median BK cluster size in hippocampal neurons (2000 nm2, n = 6) or the expression system (1600 nm2, n = 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison from the super-resolution data.

claim: In hippocampal neurons, 3% of the pixels inside BK clusters also included CaV1.3 channels.
source: Interestingly, whereas in hippocampal neurons 3% of the pixels inside BK clusters also included CaV1.3 channels, in SCG neurons as many as 10% of the BK cluster pixels included CaV1.3 channels, suggesting more intimate coupling of these interacting channels in SCG neurons.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the super-resolution data.

claim: In SCG neurons, 10% of the BK cluster pixels included CaV1.3 channels.
source: Interestingly, whereas in hippocampal neurons 3% of the pixels inside BK clusters also included CaV1.3 channels, in SCG neurons as many as 10% of the BK cluster pixels included CaV1.3 channels, suggesting more intimate coupling of these interacting channels in SCG neurons.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the super-resolution data.

claim: There is more intimate coupling of BK and CaV1.3 channels in SCG neurons compared to hippocampal neurons.
source: Interestingly, whereas in hippocampal neurons 3% of the pixels inside BK clusters also included CaV1.3 channels, in SCG neurons as many as 10% of the BK cluster pixels included CaV1.3 channels, suggesting more intimate coupling of these interacting channels in SCG neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the higher percentage of overlap in SCG neurons.

claim: Randomized CaV1.3 channel clusters were distributed independently of the position of BK channels in neurons.
source: Randomized CaV1.3 channel clusters were distributed independently of the position of BK channels in the neurons (Figure 5C,E, orange circles).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and 5E.

claim: Endogenous BK and CaV1.3 channels in neurons exhibit a distribution and coupling similar to those in the expression system.
source: Such results show that endogenous BK and CaV1.3 channels in neurons exhibit a distribution and coupling similar to those in the expression system and suggest that clustering and proximity are fundamental properties of endogenous BK and CaV1.3 channels and not an artifact of overexpression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of neuronal and expression system data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Clustering and proximity are fundamental properties of endogenous BK and CaV1.3 channels and not an artifact of overexpression.
source: Such results show that endogenous BK and CaV1.3 channels in neurons exhibit a distribution and coupling similar to those in the expression system and suggest that clustering and proximity are fundamental properties of endogenous BK and CaV1.3 channels and not an artifact of overexpression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of neuronal and expression system data.

claim: 200 ± 20 pA (n = 3) of paxilline-sensitive potassium currents were observed at −40 mV in hippocampal neurons.
source: On average, we observed 200 ± 20 pA (n = 3) of paxilline-sensitive potassium currents at −40 mV in hippocampal neurons and 100 ± 20 pA (n = 3) in sympathetic neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: 100 ± 20 pA (n = 3) of paxilline-sensitive potassium currents were observed at −40 mV in sympathetic neurons.
source: On average, we observed 200 ± 20 pA (n = 3) of paxilline-sensitive potassium currents at −40 mV in hippocampal neurons and 100 ± 20 pA (n = 3) in sympathetic neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Calcium current at −40 mV is minimal or undetectable in whole-cell recordings in hippocampal and sympathetic neurons.
source: Calcium current at −40 mV is minimal or undetectable in whole-cell recordings in hippocampal and sympathetic neurons (Regan et al., 1991; Vivas et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Activation of a few channels, or clusters, is enough to begin to activate BK channels at low voltages.
source: Nonetheless, it is possible that activation of a few channels, or clusters, is enough to begin to activate BK channels at low voltages.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism.

claim: Localized bursts of fluorescent events (sparklets) were detected in sympathetic neurons at −80 mV.
source: Localized bursts of fluorescent events were detected (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Sparklets reflect the opening of single or clustered CaV1.3 channels.
source: These events, termed sparklets, have been characterized in tsA-201 cells expressing CaV1.3 channels and are known to reflect the opening of single or clustered channels (Navedo et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Sparklets increased in number and amplitude after application of 500 nM Bay K 8644.
source: Importantly, these events increased in number and amplitude after application of 500 nM Bay K 8644 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3D), suggesting that they are mediated by L-type calcium channels.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Sparklets are mediated by L-type calcium channels.
source: Importantly, these events increased in number and amplitude after application of 500 nM Bay K 8644 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3D), suggesting that they are mediated by L-type calcium channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effect of Bay K 8644, an L-type channel agonist.

claim: SCG neurons exhibit spontaneous activity of single and coupled L-type calcium channels at negative potentials.
source: Altogether, these results show that SCG neurons exhibit spontaneous activity of single and coupled L-type calcium channels at negative potentials that can contribute to the activation of nearby BK channels even in the absence of detectable whole-cell calcium current.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the sparklet data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Spontaneous activity of L-type calcium channels can contribute to the activation of nearby BK channels even in the absence of detectable whole-cell calcium current.
source: Altogether, these results show that SCG neurons exhibit spontaneous activity of single and coupled L-type calcium channels at negative potentials that can contribute to the activation of nearby BK channels even in the absence of detectable whole-cell calcium current.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the sparklet data and the detection of BK currents at −40 mV.

claim: CaV1.3 channels couple to BK channels in multi-channel complexes.
source: We found that CaV1.3 channels couple to BK channels in multi-channel complexes, enabling BK channels to open at voltages as negative as −50 mV.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: Multi-channel complexes of CaV1.3 and BK channels enable BK channels to open at voltages as negative as −50 mV.
source: We found that CaV1.3 channels couple to BK channels in multi-channel complexes, enabling BK channels to open at voltages as negative as −50 mV.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the functional data in Figures 1 and 5.

claim: Single-molecule localization experiments did not support proposed models of strict stoichiometry such as a 1:1 ratio of CaV and BK channels.
source: Our single-molecule localization experiments did not support proposed models of strict stoichiometry such as a 1:1 ratio of CaV and BK channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the super-resolution data in Figure 4.

claim: BK channels form clusters that are surrounded by clusters of CaV1.3 channels with no apparent fixed stoichiometry.
source: Instead, we found that BK channels form clusters that are surrounded by clusters of CaV1.3 channels with no apparent fixed stoichiometry.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the super-resolution data in Figure 4.

claim: Chromaffin cells from mice lacking CaV1.3 channels exhibit smaller BK currents.
source: These findings are consistent with previous studies that show that BK channels co-precipitate with CaV1.3 channels from rat brain extracts (Grunnet and Kaufmann, 2004) and that chromaffin cells from mice lacking CaV1.3 channels exhibit smaller BK currents (Marcantoni et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BK channels start activating at around −10 mV when co-expressed with CaV2.1 channels.
source: For instance, in their work BK channels start activating at around −10 mV when co-expressed with CaV2.1 channels but start activating at around +10 mV when co-expressed with CaV1.2 channels (Berkefeld et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BK channels start activating at around +10 mV when co-expressed with CaV1.2 channels.
source: For instance, in their work BK channels start activating at around −10 mV when co-expressed with CaV2.1 channels but start activating at around +10 mV when co-expressed with CaV1.2 channels (Berkefeld et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The BK channel activation curve corresponds closely to the activation of co-expressed CaV2.2 or CaV1.3 channels.
source: In agreement, our results show that the BK channel activation curve corresponds closely to the activation of co-expressed CaV2.2 or CaV1.3 channels, respectively, and with the latter can start activating at voltages as negative as −50 mV.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: The auxiliary β subunit of BK channels is not necessary to reconstitute the functional coupling between BK and CaV channels.
source: Our experiments differ, however, in that we did not co-express the auxiliary β subunit of BK channels, suggesting that this auxiliary subunit is not necessary to reconstitute the functional coupling between BK and CaV channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the successful functional coupling observed without the β subunit.

claim: Clustering is a characteristic of several ion channels, including potassium and calcium channels.
source: Clustering is a characteristic of several ion channels, including potassium and calcium channels, (Choi, 2014; King et al., 2014; Dixon et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CaV1.3 channels form clusters that are functionally coupled to each other and gate cooperatively.
source: Recently, it was shown that CaV1.3 channels form clusters that are functionally coupled to each other and gate cooperatively (Moreno et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BK channels arrange in clusters.
source: Here we show that BK channels arrange in clusters as well and that these clusters of BK channels arrange in higher order distributions surrounded by clusters of CaV1.3 channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the super-resolution data in Figure 4.

claim: Clusters of BK channels arrange in higher order distributions surrounded by clusters of CaV1.3 channels.
source: Here we show that BK channels arrange in clusters as well and that these clusters of BK channels arrange in higher order distributions surrounded by clusters of CaV1.3 channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the super-resolution data in Figure 4.

claim: In frog hair cells, 85 calcium channels and 40 BK channels organize in the presynaptic active zone.
source: For example, in frog hair cells, it has been proposed that 85 calcium channels and 40 BK channels organize in the presynaptic active zone (Roberts, 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Assuming the simultaneous opening of 10 CaV channels at any given time, the calcium concentration could reach >100 μM inside the active zone, decaying steeply at the edge.
source: An important conclusion of that work is that, assuming the simultaneous opening of 10 CaV channels at any given time, the calcium concentration could reach >100 μM inside the active zone, decaying steeply at the edge.
evidence: This is a conclusion from cited work about calcium concentration in active zones.

claim: Others have proposed complexes with a ratio of 5:1 CaV to BK channels.
source: Others have proposed complexes with a ratio of 5:1 CaV to BK channels (Prakriya and Lingle, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Calcium channels can be at distances as far as 50 nm from BK channels and would still be able to accumulate enough calcium to activate BK channels, if more than one calcium channel opened at the same time.
source: In this case, calcium channels can be at distances as far as 50 nm from BK channels and would still be able to accumulate enough calcium to activate BK channels, if more than one calcium channel opened at the same time.
evidence: This is a theoretical consideration from cited work.

claim: The association between BK and CaV1.3 channels appears to have neither fixed stoichiometry nor fixed geometry.
source: The association we see between BK and CaV1.3 channels appears to have neither fixed stoichiometry nor fixed geometry.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the super-resolution data in Figure 4.

claim: The association between BK and CaV1.3 channels can be described as a statistical bias for proximity of clusters.
source: Rather it can be described as a statistical bias for proximity of clusters, a bias that would not be present with a random distribution.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison with randomized distributions in Figure 4D.

claim: There are on average 4 CaV1.3 clusters around a single BK cluster (n = 128 ROIs).
source: By counting the number of CaV1.3 clusters within 50 nm from BK clusters, we estimated that there are on average 4 CaV1.3 clusters around a single BK cluster (n = 128 ROIs).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the super-resolution data.

claim: The super-resolution data show considerable lack of symmetry in the BK-CaV1.3 cluster organization.
source: However, the super-resolution data show considerable lack of symmetry, with some BK clusters lacking nearby CaV1.3 clusters, CaV1.3 clusters not touching BK clusters, and CaV1.3 clusters in close proximity to BK clusters at various distances and numbers.
evidence: This is a descriptive conclusion based on the super-resolution data in Figure 4.

claim: Clustering of CaV1.3 channels leads to cooperative opening of CaV1.3 channels within the cluster.
source: Interestingly, clustering of CaV1.3 channels leads to cooperative opening of CaV1.3 channels within the cluster (Moreno et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The coupling of BK channels with low-voltage activated CaV1.3 channels in a multi-channel complex enables this feedback mechanism to activate BK channels at potentials near the threshold.
source: To conclude, we propose that the coupling of BK channels with low-voltage activated CaV1.3 channels in a multi-channel complex enables this feedback mechanism to activate BK channels at potentials near the threshold, preventing neurons from firing action potentials as we observed recently in sympathetic neurons (Vivas et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings, supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The coupling of BK channels with CaV1.3 channels prevents neurons from firing action potentials.
source: To conclude, we propose that the coupling of BK channels with low-voltage activated CaV1.3 channels in a multi-channel complex enables this feedback mechanism to activate BK channels at potentials near the threshold, preventing neurons from firing action potentials as we observed recently in sympathetic neurons (Vivas et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a proposed physiological consequence based on the experimental findings and cited previous work.
